evidence.activity: Learning and development programs for employees in cybersecurity, AI and human-centric skills, including mentor networks and early-career tracks
evidence.quote: Our learning and development programs help employees build critical capabilities in cybersecurity and AI, while strengthening human-centric skills, such as problem solving, resilience, and adaptability.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Human Capital > Onboard and Enable

community.criterion: level 2: employee development of any size (cap)

evidence.activity: Partnerships with academic institutions and other organizations to support new careers in cybersecurity
evidence.quote: To build robust talent pipelines, we partner with academic institutions and other organizations to support new careers in cybersecurity, promote open roles, proactively reach out to candidates across multiple hiring channels, and source candidates with a range of experiences.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Human Capital > Attract and Hire

community.criterion: level 2: specific current external activity, limited in reach (no figures)

evidence.activity: Investment in and support of nonprofits and initiatives that expand access to cybersecurity education for the next generation of professionals
evidence.quote: we share threat intelligence and research that helps organizations and communities better understand emerging risks, collaborate with industry partners to advance cybersecurity innovation and resilience, and invest in and support initiatives and nonprofit organizations that expand access to cybersecurity education and help develop the next generation of cybersecurity professionals.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Corporate Responsibility > Invest in People

community.criterion: level 2: specific current community investment in education, limited in reach (no figures)

evidence.activity: Giving+ program matching employees' charitable donations and volunteer time
evidence.quote: Additionally, through our Giving+ program, employees can request monetary matching of their charitable donations and volunteer time.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Human Capital > Compensation and Benefits

community.criterion: level 2: named program, limited in reach (no figures)

evidence.activity: Education services offering certifications, free online technical courses and in-classroom training to people outside the company
evidence.quote: Our education services include certifications, as well as free online technical courses and in-classroom training, which are primarily delivered through our authorized training partners.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Threat Intelligence and Advisory Services > Professional Services

community.criterion: level 2: specific current external skills offering, limited in reach (no figures)

evidence.activity: Employee Network Groups open to all employees
evidence.quote: Further providing engagement are 12 Employee Network Groups, open to all employees, that leverage different perspectives to build, understand, and support our mission.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Human Capital > Listen and Engage

cross_cultural.criterion: level 2: employee networks with no membership figures

evidence.activity: Security products sized for small businesses among other customers
evidence.quote: Our hardware and software are designed for different performance requirements throughout an organization—with the ability to secure everything from small businesses and branch offices, to large-scale data centers and service providers.
evidence.section: Item 1 > Products and Services > Next-Generation Firewalls

entrepreneurship.criterion: level 1: small-business customers with no specific enabling service

creativity.reason: Level 0: the business description covers cybersecurity and observability products only, with no creative activity; uses of 'design', 'content', 'licensing' and 'state-of-the-art' are traps.

community.reason: Level 2: specific current external education and community investment activities (academic partnerships, cybersecurity-education nonprofits, Giving+, free technical courses) plus employee development, but no participants, dollars or other reach indicators are disclosed.

cross_cultural.reason: Level 2: 12 Employee Network Groups open to all employees, with no membership figures or other reach indicators.

entrepreneurship.reason: Level 1: small businesses appear only as one customer size served, with no specific enabling program; startups are mentioned only as competitors.

ai.notes: The 'inclusion' company value and 'bias mitigation' in hiring are labels or general practice with no specific program, so they were not scored above the network groups. E2 is mainly recruitment-oriented. E5 is product-related technical training, a possible overlap with the 'educating customers' trap, but it includes free courses, so it was kept at level 2 only. No external activity discloses figures, which keeps Community at 2. Trap terms excluded: 'threat intelligence sharing community', 'huntr research community', 'investment community', 'foundation of the AI ecosystem', 'joint'/'startups' as competitors, 'identity' security products, 'diversified product lines', and end-customers in over 180 countries (international sales only). The filing references an annual Corporate Responsibility Report but also describes specific activities itself, so coverage is sufficient and no second look is triggered.
